clue.text: Play about staff caught 'returning giraffe

indicators.note: returning tells the solver to read the whole assembled string backwards
the play goes about, that is around, the staff, holding it inside

parts.note: a play is a drama
a staff is a pole
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A drama about a staff caught coming back, with a giraffe thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the staff inside the play; 'returning' then reverses everything, caught included. Camelopard is an old name for the giraffe, from camel plus leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelopard is the archaic English name for the long-necked African animal, from its supposed camel-and-leopard look.

clue.text: Natural enemy of 28

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the canines at 28-across, and the wanted creatures are their traditional household foes

explanation.surface: A naturalist names the predator of a creature listed elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Felines and canines are the proverbial sworn foes of household pets.

clue.text: Spoil football team good man too far out on left wing ?

definitions.text: too far out on left wing ?

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is the size of a football side
ST, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a football team by being too extreme on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left wing' looks like a football position, but the definition is political: a follower of Marx, too far out on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx sits at the far political left, beyond moderate socialism.

clue.text: Prominent member, like the Dong's nose

definitions.meaning: an important, influential figure in a group
Edward Lear's nonsense poem The Dong with a Luminous Nose gives its hero a glowing lamp of a nose

explanation.surface: A notable figure is likened to the glowing nose of Lear's Dong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dong with a Luminous Nose is a nonsense poem by Edward Lear; the Dong's nose glows like a lantern.
explanation.definitionFit: A key figure in a movement is called a beacon or guide, and a luminous nose literally shines ahead.

clue.text: Paperwork-—going flat out is pointless at first

indicators.note: the compass point S, south, is dropped from the front of the word

parts.note: running at top speed is sprinting

explanation.surface: Paperwork done at a frantic pace proves pointless from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless at first' removes S, a compass point, from the start of SPRINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Press work turning out copies on paper is the trade of the printer.

clue.text: Resort having the edge in Italy, initially

parts.note: an edge or border is a rim

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word Italy

explanation.surface: A seaside resort that gives Italy its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a well-known holiday town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Fellow abridging section of book

indicators.note: abridging shortens the word, cutting off its final letters as an abbreviation does

parts.note: a book is divided into chapters

explanation.surface: A man cuts down a part of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridging' cuts CHAPTER to its usual abbreviation, dropping TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man or bloke.

clue.text: One who plays his part badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor makes a hash of his role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' suggests acting, but the player plucks an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on the harp is a kind of musician who plays strings.

clue.text: Before the excitement of promotion

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a ferment is a state of agitation or excitement

explanation.surface: Anticipation builds ahead of a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank or office, especially in the church, is advancement.

clue.text: Land trip with a company in old volunteer force

indicators.note: the slip, A and business are placed inside the reserve army's letters

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army
to trip is to err, make a slip
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A trip ashore with a company of the old volunteer army.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, as opposed to sea.

clue.text: Mid-way's actor-manager

indicators.note: mid keeps only the middle of the word, dropping its first and last letters

parts.note: a way such as a road is a street

explanation.surface: A theatre impresario is halfway along his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager; 'Mid' drops the first and last letters of STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree ran Her Majesty's Theatre in London and starred in his own productions.

clue.text: Dreamer's crafty device for climbing plant

definitions.meaning: in Genesis the patriarch dreamed of a stairway to heaven, and on a ship (a craft) a rope ladder bears the same name

explanation.surface: A dreamer uses a clever gadget to scale a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' hints at a ship: a rope ladder with wooden rungs on a vessel shares the Biblical name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical dream ladder names both a ship's rope ladder and the flowering perennial Polemonium.

clue.text: Man in Wellington unable to take off

definitions.meaning: a New Zealander, Wellington being the country's capital
describes the flightless national bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A man in boots cannot get his footwear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' suggests a rubber boot, but it is New Zealand's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird is the national symbol, and its name is slang for any New Zealander.

clue.text: Number four in the gallery is experimental

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: the Roman four goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fourth exhibit in the gallery is experimental art.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tentative is a trial, provisional and not yet settled.

clue.text: Nightwatchman's job for a scoundrel ?

parts.note: a watchman on duty in the dark could be called a guard of the night, read as two words describing his post

explanation.surface: A villain takes work as a night watchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackguard is a rogue or villain, the word once naming kitchen menials.

clue.text: Titling a novel " Man of Action '

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An author names a novel Man of Action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram; 'Action' is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings or defends a lawsuit is a party to legal proceedings.

clue.text: Contract Thomas doubled can be beaten

indicators.note: doubled means the shortened name is written out twice
to contract a name is to shorten it, here dropping its later letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A contract with Thomas, doubled, can still be bettered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' shortens THOMAS to TOM, and 'doubled' repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a drum, something hollow struck with the hands or sticks.

clue.text: Fine stuff, and very valuable

definitions.meaning: particles of the precious metal, fine as powder
as in the idiom like ..., meaning scarce and prized

explanation.surface: Something fine and precious indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered precious metal is literally fine, and the idiom 'like gold dust' means highly prized.

clue.text: One Pole associated with many a dance

definitions.text: One Pole associated with many a dance

parts.words: One Pole associated with many a dance
parts.note: a Polish composer famed for mazurkas, polonaises and waltzes

explanation.surface: A Polish man is linked with plenty of dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin, the Polish composer, wrote numerous waltzes, mazurkas and polonaises.

clue.text: Pawn gone, in mishandling this ?

indicators.note: mishandling means the letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player loses a pawn by botching the start of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishandling' rearranges P plus GONE IN; the whole clue describes a chess gambit, an opening that gives up a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The first moves of a chess game are its opening, and gambits sacrifice a pawn.

clue.text: Christ Church graduate in hospital?

parts.note: Christ Church, Oxford, is nicknamed the House, so its member could be a man of the House; a new doctor in hospital

explanation.surface: An Oxford graduate ends up in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Christ Church, an Oxford college, is known as 'the House'.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior doctor resident in a hospital is a house officer, and the college pun fits too.

clue.text: I'm turning up with Ulysses, travelling from country to country

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the little word from bottom to top

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant was the US general and president

explanation.surface: I appear with Ulysses on his wanderings abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulysses' suggests the wandering Greek hero, but it is Ulysses S. Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person who moves between countries.

clue.text: Painter portrays 14's latter half with one

indicators.note: only the second half of the word is kept, the first half dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter portrays the second half of a scoundrel with one more.
explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Guardi was an 18th-century Venetian view painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Guardi painted Venetian vedute in the 1700s.

clue.text: Sea-dog, on the ocean ?

parts.note: a fast ocean liner was called a racing dog of the ocean, the dog being the sea-coloured hound

explanation.surface: An old sailor out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-dog' suggests an old sailor; the racing dog shares its colour with a grey sea, and fast liners were 'ocean greyhounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift racing hound, and fast liners were called greyhounds of the sea.

clue.text: Special terms, we hear, for Greek ship

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another, the final T of the French word being silent

parts.note: argot is jargon, a group's special vocabulary

explanation.surface: We hear some special terms used for a Greek vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Argot is pronounced without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: He ousts man from seat, without support

indicators.note: ousts means the word is thrown out of the longer one

parts.note: an ottoman is a low upholstered seat with no back or arms
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone evicts a man from his chair, leaving him unsupported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: Otto is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a German male name, so a fellow called this is a he.

clue.text: Settled sale, with contents

indicators.note: contents means the insides of each word, without their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sale is settled, contents included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' takes AL from sale and IT from with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that has landed on a perch has alighted, past tense of alight.

clue.text: Needed to get big tuna with rod, perhaps.

definitions.text: Needed to get big tuna with rod, perhaps.

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An angler explains what is needed to land a big tuna with a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BIG TUNA and ROD rearranged; the whole clue describes what anglers scatter to draw fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbait is food thrown into water to attract fish to the angler's hook.

clue.text: Following 1dn, falling heavily

parts.note: the idiom for a downpour pairs the felines at 1-down with a second kind of pet after the word and

explanation.surface: Something comes after an earlier entry and pours down hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'raining cats and dogs' means pouring with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom about heavy rain ends with canines after the felines.

clue.text: Painter needs money to return fur

parts.note: tin is British slang for money

indicators.note: return means the fur's name is read backwards

parts.note: otter is a fur from the river animal

explanation.surface: A painter needs money to get back his fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a Venetian Renaissance painter of the 1500s.
